newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks bolstered at close by mild inflation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks bolstered at close by mild inflation.

text.p: Mexican stocks moderated earlier gains at the close on Wednesday, but shrugged off a downturn on Wall Street after lower-than-expected inflation data were released, traders and analysts said.
"The bourse began to slide on the Dow, but Telmex closed very firm and inflation figures also helped at the close," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 12.99 points, or 0.34 percent, at 3,797.30, down from an earlier high of 3,809.95. The Dow Jones meanwhile ended down 45.32 points at 6,563.84.
Banco de Mexico announced in late trade that the March consumer price index had slowed to a 1.24 percent rise, from 1.68 in February.
This compares with an average forecast of 1.31 percent in consumer prices in a previous Reuters survey of Mexico City financial houses.
"Inflation has been tamed...interest rates may have gained recently, but they're not out of control," said Ramon Ruiz, of the equity sales department at Latinvest in New York.
Trading volume was lacklustre at 78.96 million shares traded.

"The market is out of gas as there are no foreign investors dealing," an equity analyst said. "Volatility on Wall Street is still infectious, and the bourse will continue to be erratic as long as that is the case."
Traders said telecom Telmex and retail chain Cifra weighed most on the upside during the session.
Telmex L shares gained 10 centavos to 15.88 pesos, paralleling its ADRs, which ended up 3/8 at 40-3/8.
Cifra B B climbed 30 centavos to 11.20 pesos, while its C shares were also up 30 centavos to 11.10 pesos.
Traders said Cifra gained on a technical rebound. The two Cifra share series and Telmex accounted for 26 percent of all shares traded.
Financial group GFB B shares were heavily traded decliners, down five centavos to 2.72 pesos in response to increased primary interest rates.
Market heavyweight Cemex ended down 55 centavos to 28.45 pesos on technical factors, traders said.
GFB and cement maker Cemex together accounted for 21 percent of all shares traded.
On the broad market, 105 stocks changed hands, with decliners outnumbering gainers by 46 to 34.
Construction company Consorcio Ara gained one peso to 28.35 pesos and ended near the top of the prominent gainers' list.
"Very good earnings for the first quarter of 1997 are expected," said Monica Lourdes, an analyst at the BBV-Probursa brokerage.
Retail group Salinas y Rocha posted strong gains for the fourth session in a row, ending up six centavos at 66 centavos.

"Market speculation is awful, it can greatly move a stock for no fundamental reason. With the recent Sears deal, traders are obviously talking about a possible sale of Salinas and Rocha. That's why it's been hot," a desk trader said.
Last week Sears Roebuck and Co sold a 60 percent stake in Sears de Mexico to the Grupo Carso holding group.
Cement makers Grupo Cementos de Chihuahua (GCC) headed the leading decliners, down 24 centavos to 7.50 pesos.
Traders noted GCC would be hit more than other leading Mexican cement makers by the U.S. Department of Commerce decision last week to raise anti-dumping tariffs.
((-- Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
